messages.subject: Clarification based on validation
parts:
Hai INLA team members

I have run a model based on spatial-temporal for training data set (Jan 2013 – Dec 2018) using the following script and saved the .RData

  training_model <- inla(formula,

              distribution,

              data= data,

              E = E,

              control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE, cdf=c(log(1))),

              control.compute=list(dic=TRUE, waic=TRUE, cpo = TRUE, config = TRUE),

              control.fixed= list(prec.intercept = 1, prec=1),

              control.inla = list(tolerance=1e-6, strategy =strategy, int.strategy = "eb", cmin=0),

              lincomb=all.lc,

              verbose = T)

 

Now I am interested to validate the model for the test period (Jan 2019 to Dec 2020) by assigning ‘NA’ using

 

data$count[data$year%in%c((2019:2020))] <- NA

I have used the following script for validating the model:

 Test_model <- inla(formula,

                             distribution,

                             data= data,

                             E = E,

                            control.mode(result =   training_model, restart = T),

                            control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE, cdf=c(log(1))),

                            control.compute=list(dic=TRUE, waic=TRUE, cpo = TRUE,config = TRUE),

                           control.fixed= list(prec.intercept = 1, prec=1),

                           control.inla = list(tolerance=1e-6, strategy =strategy, int.strategy = "eb", cmin = 0),

                           lincomb=all.lc,

                            verbose = T)

 

I would request your advice on the following question:

While running inla for test period, should I load the .Rdata (obtained from fitting model to the training dataset)? or directly run the inla without calling .Rdata?
